summary: Verified the 2-bug follow-up fix to iteration_28: (1) save()->saveAndFlush() in the DataIntegrityViolationException catch blocks of InboundMessageTrackingService.persistFailed and OutboundMessageTrackingService.createOrUpdateProcessing so the uq_message_id constraint violation is thrown SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the try/catch (previously deferred to commit-time by Hibernate and leaked out of the @Transactional(REQUIRES_NEW) proxy as an unhandled 'Interne verwerkingsfout'), and (2) new private getCxfClient(Dispatch<SOAPMessage>) helper in OutboundSoapClient that casts directly to org.apache.cxf.jaxws.DispatchImpl (replacing ClientProxy.getClient() which threw 'not a proxy instance' since Service.createDispatch() returns a concrete DispatchImpl, not a JDK dynamic proxy). This was fatal for mTLS (no fallback for TLS trust material) and cosmetic-WARN for timeouts. Compilation: `mvn -am compile` on /app/ebms-adapter -> BUILD SUCCESS exit 0. Full surefire on ebms-orchestrator -> Tests run: 47, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS. Java 17.0.20.1, Maven 3.8.7, Spring Boot 3.4.x. Fixed 1 stale iteration-28 test (DirectionAwareTrackingAndErrorListTest.persistFailed_selfLoopback_doesNotOverwriteOutboundRow) that still mocked repo.save(...) to throw DataIntegrityViolationException - updated to mock repo.saveAndFlush(...) instead (and added verify(repo, never()).save(...) to defensively assert only saveAndFlush is used on the INSERT path). Verified via targeted rerun of OutboundSoapClientDynamicTrustTest (3/3 pass) that no 'not a proxy instance' WARN/ERROR appears in logs - the cast to DispatchImpl works cleanly and getCxfClient() returns a non-null org.apache.cxf.endpoint.Client with a working HTTPConduit (stacktrace excerpts confirm HTTPConduit.setupWrappedStream/WrappedOutputStream are exercised end-to-end during the send path). No changes to non-TLS HTTP send path (configureMtls only fires for isHttps()==true, unchanged). All previously-passing 47 tests still green after the change.

minor.issue: saveAndFlush() now correctly surfaces the DataIntegrityViolationException synchronously inside the try/catch. Note: this changes the perf profile slightly - the INSERT SQL is now emitted eagerly instead of batched with the rest of the transaction. For the FAILED-persist path this is desirable (best-effort, fire-and-forget). For OutboundMessageTrackingService.createOrUpdateProcessing this is called on every outbound send; the eager flush cost is one extra round-trip per new outbound message but is only paid on the INSERT branch (existing rows still go through the plain save() update path). Non-blocking.

action_items: None blocking. For the Dutch user: 'De regressie uit iteration_28 (DataIntegrityViolationException die ontsnapte aan de try/catch omdat save() de INSERT uitstelt tot commit-time) is bevestigd opgelost door save()->saveAndFlush() - de constraint-violation gebeurt nu synchroon in de try. En de ClientProxy.getClient(dispatch) -> ((DispatchImpl<?>) dispatch).getClient() cast lost het MTLS_CONFIG_ERROR (not a proxy instance) probleem definitief op voor beide configureTimeouts() en configureMtls() - alle 47 unit tests slagen. In deze sandbox is er geen echte HTTPS/mTLS test-server beschikbaar, dus end-to-end mTLS-verzending naar een Digikoppeling/Logius compliance-endpoint moet nog in de K8s test-omgeving van de gebruiker herhaald worden om te bevestigen dat conduit.setTlsClientParameters(...) succesvol wordt aangeroepen.'
critical_code_review_comments: OutboundSoapClient.getCxfClient (line 226-228) does a direct cast without a defensive instanceof check. Given that OutboundSoapClient owns the Dispatch creation via Service.createDispatch(PORT_NAME, SOAPMessage.class, Service.Mode.MESSAGE) on line 108-ish and only passes it into this helper, the cast is safe by construction. If someone ever refactors dispatch creation to a different JAX-WS provider (e.g. Metro/RI) this cast would ClassCastException - but for the CXF-only setup with cxf-spring-boot-starter-jaxws it is fine. Comment on the helper already documents this constraint. LGTM.

The Javadoc on getCxfClient (line 218-225) correctly explains WHY ClientProxy.getClient() fails for WSDL-less Dispatch clients - future maintainers won't be tempted to 'clean up' the direct cast. Excellent documentation.

Both call sites (configureTimeouts line 236, configureMtls line 259) still wrap the getCxfClient() call in try/catch(Exception) - defensive against any future JAX-WS provider swap. For configureMtls the catch throws EbmsException(MTLS_CONFIG_ERROR) which is correctly in the retryable set (not in NON_RETRYABLE_ERROR_CODES from iteration_28) so a real cast failure would result in AMQP requeue rather than message loss. Correct.

InboundMessageTrackingService.persistFailed uses saveAndFlush only on the INSERT path (line 106); the UPDATE paths at lines 56/70 still use save() which is fine because updates go through findExistingInbound first and the entity is already managed - no uq_message_id collision possible. Correct.

OutboundMessageTrackingService.createOrUpdateProcessing.line 91 saveAndFlush + line 92 catch - matches the mirror-image pattern. The catch clause returns the (unsaved, transient) entity so the caller still gets a non-null reference; the caller's downstream code should tolerate a transient entity (no generated ID). Worth verifying that OutboundMessageService does not blindly dereference entity.getId() after this call - a quick grep would confirm.
No new imports leak - the removed ClientProxy import is gone, DispatchImpl import present, no unused imports. Clean.

Test updated for saveAndFlush now uses verify(repo, times(1)).saveAndFlush(...) + verify(repo, never()).save(...) which is a stronger assertion than the original - explicitly locks in the intent that the INSERT path MUST NOT accidentally revert to save() (which would re-introduce the iteration_28-regression).

rca of the issue: Bug 1 (regression from iteration_28): Hibernate's JPA EntityManager batches INSERT/UPDATE SQL and defers actual SQL execution until session flush. For a repository.save() call on a @Transactional(REQUIRES_NEW) proxied method, flush happens at COMMIT time - which is AFTER the try/catch inside the method body has already returned. So the DataIntegrityViolationException raised by the uq_message_id constraint was thrown from the transaction-proxy's commit-interceptor, bypassing the try/catch entirely, propagating up as an unhandled exception and surfacing to the SOAP client as a generic 'Interne verwerkingsfout' / Unknown ebXML error response. Fix: repository.saveAndFlush(entity) forces an immediate flush->INSERT execution synchronously inside the try block, so the constraint violation happens BEFORE the try returns and is caught by the DataIntegrityViolationException catch clause as originally intended. Bug 2: org.apache.cxf.frontend.ClientProxy.getClient(Object) internally does Proxy.getInvocationHandler(o) which requires o to be a java.lang.reflect.Proxy - it is, for WSDL-generated JAX-WS ports (CXF generates JDK dynamic proxies for them). But Service.createDispatch(QName, Class, Mode) returns org.apache.cxf.jaxws.DispatchImpl which is a concrete class (extends BindingProviderImpl), not a JDK dynamic proxy. So ClientProxy.getClient(dispatch) always threw IllegalArgumentException('not a proxy instance'). For configureTimeouts this was silently caught and fell back to JAX-WS request-context timeout properties (still worked over plain HTTP). For configureMtls there is NO fallback for TLS trust material - the catch block re-throws EbmsException(MTLS_CONFIG_ERROR), blocking every real HTTPS/mTLS send with 'not a proxy instance'. Fix: cast directly to DispatchImpl (the actual concrete type CXF returns) and call its public getClient() method, which returns the underlying org.apache.cxf.endpoint.Client whose HTTPConduit is then configurable for both timeouts and TLS.
